newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian tribes agree to end Kalimantan riots.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian tribes agree to end Kalimantan riots.

text.p: Two Indonesian tribes have agreed to put an end to recent ethnic clashes in West Kalimantan province in which 12 people were reported killed, the official Antara news agency reported on Sunday.

The agency said community leaders of the native Dayak tribe and migrants from Madura island off the main island of Java vowed on Saturday to end their disputes at a ceremony held at army headquarters in Pontianak, capital of West Kalimantan.
"Community leaders from both parties agree that the clashes have disturbed the unity and caused losses in property and life," said the agency.
Antara said thousands of people witnessed the ceremony, but it gave no further details.

Violence erupted in the province, on the Indonesian side of Borneo island, late in December between Dayaks and Maduran migrants. The clash in Sanggau Ledo, about 95 km (60 miles), north of Pontianak, was apparently sparked by a fight over a girl.
Further violence rooted in long-standing ethnic rivalry resumed in late January and continued as recently as last month. About 3,000 troops were deployed to contain unrest.
The military and local residents have said at least 12 people died during the riots.
